junction.name: Northeast 50th Street & University Way Northeast, Seattle

claims.text: Northeast 50th Street & University Way Northeast had 54 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $3.7 million a year.
21% of crashes here had “hit a parked car” recorded as a contributing factor, against 10% at the city's worst crash locations.
17% of crashes here were recorded as “parked car” crashes, against 10% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: national studies only), worth $402,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.6 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $555,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 15th Avenue Northeast, Northeast 50th Street, University Way Northeast (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
